audit.why: Akshan owns levels 2 through first item on range and the Dirty Fighting double-shot; Ryze reclaims the lane at two-plus items. The existing text says this and the packet levelChart agrees. Avengerang is 850 base range and extends per enemy hit, against Ryze's 615-range Spell Flux and Rune Prison — that range gap is the whole early lane.
audit.corrected: Re-anchored the early and mid text to real ranges (850 vs 615) and Spell Flux's 3.5s cooldown so the spacing advice is measurable.

audit.why: Spikes are level 2-3 (Q max value plus Heroic Swing), level 6 Comeuppance, first-item lethality, and Ryze's two-plus item Tear spike. Comeuppance is 100s at rank 1 and scales off the target's missing health, so it is a finisher, not an opener — the entry already frames it that way.
audit.corrected: No count change. Left the four spikes intact and sharpened whys[3] and the cooldown block with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Rune Prison a 'point-and-click root' and repeatedly describes an 'E-Q root chain'. Both are wrong.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' The root is conditional on Spell Flux (E) being on you, and it comes from W, not Q. Overload's extra effect against a Fluxed target is damage, not CC. So dodging the 615-range, 3.5s-cooldown E turns Rune Prison into a slow — and a slow does not end Heroic Swing.
audit.corrected: Stated the Flux-then-W root condition in early, winCon, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], whys[3], dosFull[2].d, breakdown.cooldowns and loading. Also added Heroic Swing's real requirement — a terrain anchor — and that champion collision knocks him off the arc.

audit.why: Rune Prison is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 615 range; Spell Flux is 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5s. The short cooldown on E is why 'wait for his root to be down' is unusable advice — the correct read is whether Flux is on you right now.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns with both numbers and added Heroic Swing 18s / Comeuppance 100s so the budget line has timers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry says Heroic Swing requires terrain to anchor to, or that it ends on champion collision.
audit.why: Riot: 'Akshan fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... he gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain.' Against an immobile mage this is the difference between a free trade and standing still in his face.

edits.before: Ryze's early threat is the root: his E (Spell Flux) tags you, then Q (Overload) snaps the root for a free combo, and his W (Rune Prison) is a separate point-and-click root if you dive in carelessly. But he's a slow, immobile mage with no dash — Flash is his only out, which is exactly your meal. Last-hit at Q range and fire a boomerang every time he walks up to CS, and your double-shot passive chips him on top. Don't facetank his E-Q chain: sidestep the E so the root never lands, and he can't punish your poke. At level 1 you only have your passive second shot and Q, so don't over-step before you hit 2.
edits.after: Ryze's early threat is one sequence: Spell Flux (E) tags you, then Rune Prison (W) roots instead of slowing. With no Flux on you that W is only a slow, so dodging the 615-range E defuses the chain outright. He's immobile with no dash and Flash is his only out, which is exactly your meal. Last-hit at Avengerang range — 850 to his 615 — and throw it every step-up, since both passes hit and the double-shot passive chips on top. Spell Flux is back every 3.5s, so sidestep it on his walk-up, not on a cooldown count. At level 1 you have only the second shot and Q, so don't over-step before 2.

edits.before: Sidestep his E (Spell Flux) so the E-Q root chain never lands and W is his only catch tool
edits.after: Sidestep Spell Flux (E) — with no Flux on you, Rune Prison (W) only slows and never ends your swing

edits.before: Land E (Spell Flux) into Q (Overload) to root you out of Heroic Swing, then chunk you with his spell-reset combo
edits.after: Land Spell Flux (E) then Rune Prison (W) — the Flux upgrades that slow into the root that ends Heroic Swing mid-arc

edits.before: These are your strongest pure-laning levels: your Q-plus-passive trades out-damage his poke and he can't punish your range without first landing the E-Q root.
edits.after: These are your strongest pure-laning levels: your Q-plus-passive trades out-damage his poke and he can't punish your range without landing Flux, then Rune Prison.

edits.before: Out-angle the poke war and execute the chip with R. Nothing here works through Rune Prison (Root) — schedule your pattern around its cooldown.
edits.after: Out-angle the poke war and execute the chip with R. Rune Prison only roots you if Spell Flux landed first — dodge the E and his W is just a slow.

edits.before: Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Heroic Swing needs terrain, and champion collision ends the arc — swing past him, never into him.

edits.before: Ryze spends Rune Prison (Root) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Bait Spell Flux out first — no Flux on you means Rune Prison only slows, and your channel lives.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E swing for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Rune Prison (W): 11s at rank 1, 615 range — it only roots through a Spell Flux debuff, so dodging the 3.5s E disarms it. - Budget Heroic Swing (18s) for emergencies and Comeuppance (100s) for opportunities — never swap them.

edits.before: - Akshan vs Ryze - Track: Ryze Rune Prison (Root). - Three hits and out — never flat trades. - Rune Prison (Root) down is the green light. - Hold the ult for names, not waves.
edits.after: - Akshan vs Ryze - Track: Ryze Spell Flux (E, 3.5s). - Three hits and out — never flat trades. - No Flux on you means no root — step up. - Hold the ult for names, not waves.

notes:
The 'E-Q root chain' framing is a systemic error and likely appears in every Akshan-vs-Ryze-style entry generated from the same template: Ryze's root is Spell Flux (E) followed by Rune Prison (W). Overload's bonus against a Fluxed target is damage, granted by his R passive, not crowd control. Worth a site-wide grep for 'E-Q root'.
